subject: social
title: Holidays and Traditions
about: What holidays, traditions and culture are, which national and cultural holidays we celebrate and why, and the arts and stories different cultures share. NC 1.B.1.1, 1.B.1.2 and 1.B.1.3.
tip: Before a holiday, ask him what it celebrates and name one family tradition you have for it.

cards.q: A special day that people celebrate is a...
cards.note: Independence Day and Thanksgiving are holidays.

cards.q: Something a family does the same way every year is a...
cards.note: Eating the same special meal every year is a tradition.

cards.q: The food, clothes, music and celebrations of a group of people are their...
cards.note: Every family has a culture, and families share it with each other.

cards.q: Which holiday on July 4 has fireworks and celebrates the birthday of the USA?
cards.note: The USA began on July 4, 1776. Many people call it the Fourth of July.

cards.q: Which November holiday is for giving thanks with a big meal?
cards.note: Thanksgiving is on the fourth Thursday in November.

cards.q: Which holiday on January 1 celebrates a brand new year?
cards.note: The night before, people count down to midnight.

cards.q: On which February holiday do people give cards and hearts to people they love?
cards.note: Valentine's Day is February 14.

cards.q: Which April holiday reminds us to take care of our planet?
cards.note: Earth Day is April 22. Many people plant trees or pick up litter.

cards.q: Which January holiday remembers a leader who worked for fairness for all people?
cards.note: Dr. King gave speeches so that all people would be treated fairly.

cards.q: On which November holiday do we thank people who served in the military?
cards.note: Veterans Day is November 11. A veteran is a person who served in the military.

cards.q: Which June 19 holiday celebrates freedom and the end of slavery?
cards.note: The name Juneteenth mixes the words June and nineteenth.

cards.q: Which May 5 celebration honors Mexican culture?
cards.note: Cinco de Mayo means the fifth of May in Spanish. People enjoy music, food and dancing.

cards.q: Which holiday do many families celebrate with lion dances and red envelopes?
cards.note: Lunar New Year comes in January or February. Red is a lucky color.

cards.q: Each October a big fair with rides and farm animals comes to Raleigh. It is the...
cards.note: The NC State Fair happens every October in Raleigh, our state capital.

cards.q: Blowing out candles on a cake is a tradition for a...
cards.note: A birthday celebrates the day you were born.

cards.q: An old story told again and again, passed down from long ago, is a...
cards.note: Many folktales have talking animals. The Little Red Hen is one.

cards.q: Folding paper into animals and shapes, a tradition from Japan, is...
cards.note: Origami cranes and frogs are folded from one square of paper.

cards.q: A blanket sewn from many pieces of cloth is a...
cards.note: Many quilts are sewn by hand and passed down in families.

cards.q: People in a community can come from many different...
cards.note: Neighbors may speak different languages and eat different foods.

cards.q: How should we treat people whose traditions are different from ours?
cards.note: We can ask kind questions to learn about new traditions.
